hx_moments_any_xld — 2D halcon_ext op

• Data kinds: contour → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "hx_moments_any_xld", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: moments_any_xld (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*Knob a does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

*Knob b does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

Stages (the ops that come before → this op, left to right):

▸ hx_moments_any_xld: stages (docs site)

Usage

The second central moment (the spread) of all contour points, as a normalised feature.

Pools all points of the contour dict and takes the mean squared distance from the centroid mean((row - mean_row)^2 + (col - mean_col)^2) (the 2nd-order central moment mu20 + mu02 divided by the number of points), divides it by max(H, W)^2, caps at 1 and returns it as np.float64.

• a, b are unused.

• 0.0 if there are fewer than 2 points.

An isotropic measure of "how far the point set spreads from its centroid"; orientation and aspect ratio are not included. It depends on the point density of the contour, so the value changes for the same shape if the point spacing is uneven. Oriented inertia (major/minor axis) is hx_fit_ellipse_contour / elliptic_axis_xld; the 2nd-order moments of a region are moments_region_2nd.

Try it in Studio

The program below has been verified to run (same input as the figure). In Studio's help this block becomes buttons that load and run it on the spot.

threshold 0.50 0.50
sk_find_contours 0.50 0.50
hx_moments_any_xld 0.50 0.50
